task_description: Continue debugging and completing authentication for a FastAPI student-records API after an agent handoff.

agent_a_conversation.content: Build and stabilize the student-records API for the registrar office. Keep the existing database schema and all CRUD behavior intact — we cannot afford a migration rewrite this sprint. The API must run against PostgreSQL in staging and production.

Understood. I chose FastAPI with PostgreSQL because the project needs Python integration, async I/O for concurrent reads during registration week, and relational data with foreign keys between students, enrollments, and courses. I will not touch the existing Alembic revision that created the students table.
Good. Authentication is new scope for this milestone — nothing in the repo handles login yet. Do not break the existing student CRUD endpoints while you add it.

Plan: add JWT-based auth with a /auth/login route, protect write endpoints first, and leave read endpoints open until we confirm requirements. I will use python-jose for token signing and passlib with bcrypt for password hashing — bcrypt is widely supported in our deployment images and fast enough for login traffic.
Sounds reasonable. We tried argon2 in another service but ops asked us to stay on bcrypt for consistency across internal APIs.

Noted — bcrypt it is. I implemented the SQLAlchemy models for Student and a stub User model aligned with the existing schema. The student CRUD routes live in app/routers/students.py and match the OpenAPI spec the frontend team already integrated against.
Did you get local dev running?

Yes. docker-compose brings up PostgreSQL 15 and the API on port 8000. I added a seed script that inserts two sample students. GET /students and GET /students/{id} both return 200 with the expected JSON shape.
What about SQLite for local-only dev? Some teammates prefer not running Docker.

SQLite was tried initially but abandoned because PostgreSQL is required — we rely on UUID columns, timestamptz defaults, and a partial unique index that SQLite does not emulate cleanly. Staging parity matters more than zero-dependency local setup, so docker-compose stays the supported path.
Agreed. Stick with PostgreSQL. Also please do not rename any routes; the frontend has hard-coded paths.

Route names are frozen. I implemented POST /students, PUT /students/{id}, and DELETE /students/{id} using Pydantic v2 request models. Validation errors correctly return 422. Unit tests cover the happy paths for all three verbs.
Nice. I also like the clean API naming — very readable. Anyway, where are we on auth?

Partial progress. app/auth/jwt.py can mint and decode tokens. app/auth/deps.py defines get_current_user. I have not wired login yet. First I attempted to wrap the entire FastAPI app with a global authentication middleware before adding /auth/login — that failed because every request, including health checks and the login route itself, started returning 401. I removed that middleware; do not reintroduce global middleware without exempt paths.
Good catch. Use dependency injection on specific routes instead.

Exactly what I switched to. Next step is Depends(get_current_user) on mutating student routes only. I also need a users table seed with a bcrypt hash for integration tests — the migration already exists from a prior sprint but no row is inserted yet.
Before you protect routes, run POST /students without a token and tell me what happens. That is the regression I care about most.

Running curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/students with a valid JSON body and no Authorization header returns HTTP 500, not 401 or 422. Response body: {"detail":"Internal Server Error"}. Server log shows: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'id' in app/routers/students.py line 47 inside create_student.
That is wrong — unauthenticated writes should fail closed with 401 once auth is wired, but they definitely should not 500 today while auth is still incomplete.

I agree. Line 47 currently does current_user.id for audit logging even when get_current_user is optional and returns None for missing tokens. That is likely the immediate crash, but I have not confirmed whether authentication middleware or dependency wiring is also involved.
Investigate authentication as a possible cause before changing business logic. Do not change the database schema to work around this.

Constraint acknowledged: no schema changes, preserve CRUD behavior, PostgreSQL only. I re-read students.py — create_student declares user: User | None = Depends(get_current_user). get_current_user raises HTTPException 401 when the header is missing, but optional_auth=True path returns None. The route signature may still be wrong. I have not finished tracing dependency order.
Keep the investigation focused. We can refactor audit logging after the 500 is understood.
I duplicated the failing curl five times — same 500 each time. GET endpoints still work. DELETE without auth also 500s with a similar NoneType traceback, so the bug is not isolated to POST.
What does pytest show right now?

pytest tests/unit/test_students.py — 14 passed. Those tests mock get_current_user with a fake User, so they never hit the None path. There is no integration test yet for unauthenticated POST /students, which is why this regression slipped through. I started sketching tests/integration/test_auth.py but did not commit it because login is not wired.
Does the OpenAPI page still load?

Yes — /docs renders and lists all student routes. The authorize button appears because OAuth2PasswordBearer is registered, but there is no working token endpoint to feed it yet. This is cosmetic only; the 500 reproduces outside Swagger with plain curl.

I added temporary logging in get_current_user: for requests without Authorization, it logs current_user=None before create_student runs. That confirms the dependency returns None rather than raising 401 on the code path we hit. I have not changed production logic yet — only debug prints locally.
Good. Again, no schema changes to patch this. If you need a migration for auth, that is a separate approved ticket — not for this bugfix.

No migrations planned. The users table already exists from revision a4c1f2. I only need a seed row for tests, not a new column or index. PostgreSQL stays the sole supported database — I will not revisit SQLite or add a second engine configuration.
Our standup is at 10:30 tomorrow — please have a clear status by then. Side note: cafeteria added oat milk lattes, finally.

For standup: CRUD is done, auth is half-wired, blocker is unauthenticated POST /students returning HTTP 500 instead of a controlled 401 or successful create. I will document the NoneType traceback path for whoever continues. Oat milk noted.
Walk me through the repo layout so the next person is not lost.

app/main.py mounts routers and configures OAuth2 scheme. app/routers/students.py holds create_student where line 47 writes audit metadata. app/auth/deps.py has get_current_user with an optional_auth flag. app/auth/jwt.py handles encode/decode. tests/unit mocks auth; docker-compose.yml starts db plus api. Alembic versions live under alembic/versions/. No separate service layer — routes talk to SQLAlchemy sessions directly per existing convention.
Could the OAuth2PasswordBearer auto_error setting be involved?

Possibly. oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl='/auth/login', auto_error=False) is configured in deps.py, but create_student still assumes a User when logging created_by. I have not verified whether auto_error=False combined with optional_auth=True is the intended interim behavior or a misconfiguration. That investigation is still open.
Staging deploy is blocked until QA can POST without a token and get a predictable status code.

Understood — staging stays blocked on the POST /students 500. GET traffic could theoretically ship, but ops wants the whole API held until mutating routes behave. I will not cut a hotfix branch that skips auth testing.
Remind me what is done versus open?

Completed: database models, student CRUD endpoints, docker-compose dev environment, Alembic alignment, Pydantic request/response models, unit tests for CRUD happy paths, JWT helper module, auth dependency skeleton. Not done: /auth/login, wiring Depends correctly on protected routes, integration tests for auth, fixing the unauthenticated 500 on POST /students (and likely PUT/DELETE).
Do not redo the CRUD work — it passed review. Focus on auth and the 500.

Understood. I will not rewrite models or rename routes. Remaining work: diagnose the 500 on unauthenticated mutating requests, implement JWT login, finish route-level auth dependencies, seed a test user, and expand the test suite.
What decisions are locked in?
Locked decisions: FastAPI + PostgreSQL; JWT auth; bcrypt via passlib; route-level Depends instead of global middleware; keep existing schema and OpenAPI paths; docker-compose for local dev.
Any dead ends I should know about?

Two failed approaches: SQLite local dev — abandoned because PostgreSQL-specific types and indexes are required; global auth middleware — removed because it blocked /health and /auth/login with 401 before those routes existed.
Good. What is the very next thing you would do if you kept going?

Step through get_current_user and create_student with logging, reproduce the NoneType in a minimal test, and verify whether missing Authorization should return 401 or allow anonymous create per interim policy. Current state: POST /students returns HTTP 500 for an unauthenticated request; server traceback points to audit logging using current_user.id when current_user is None.
Again — do not change the schema. Do not break existing student CRUD endpoints that already work for authenticated flows in unit tests.

Constraints restated: schema frozen, CRUD behavior preserved, PostgreSQL only, investigate auth wiring before business-logic edits. Pending: login route, middleware-free protection, auth integration tests, fix 500 on unauthenticated POST /students.
The 500 on POST /students is the blocker for QA sign-off. Everything else waits behind that.
Agreed — the unauthenticated POST /students HTTP 500 is the active blocker. JWT login and full test coverage follow once mutating routes fail predictably.
I also like the clean API naming, and the weather is finally nice today — perfect day for a walk after this deploy.

Noted on the naming feedback. Current state summary for handoff: FastAPI student-records API on PostgreSQL; CRUD and models implemented; JWT auth partially built; global middleware attempt reverted; unauthenticated POST /students (and likely PUT/DELETE) returns 500 due to NoneType in audit logging path; remaining work is investigate auth dependency wiring, implement /auth/login, protect routes, and add tests.
Please repeat the constraints one more time — I want them in the handoff notes.

Constraints: do not change the existing database schema; do not break existing student CRUD endpoints or rename routes; use PostgreSQL not SQLite; do not bring back global authentication middleware; investigate authentication dependency wiring before editing business logic in students.py.
And the failed approaches?

Failed approach one: SQLite for local dev — abandoned, PostgreSQL-specific features required. Failed approach two: global auth middleware — reverted, it 401'd /health and login. Do not retry either without explicit approval.
My kid's soccer game ran long last night so I skimmed the thread — is the 500 still the main issue?

Yes — still the main issue. POST /students without Authorization header returns HTTP 500 with AttributeError on current_user.id at line 47. PUT and DELETE show the same pattern. Everything else is secondary until that is understood.
Do we need Redis for token blocklisting?

Out of scope for this milestone. We are doing stateless JWT with short expiry only — no Redis, no refresh tokens, no logout blocklist. If security review demands revocation later, that is a new ticket.
One more time — what should the next engineer do first?

Next action: investigate whether authentication dependency wiring (optional vs required get_current_user) is causing the HTTP 500 on POST /students before making any schema or route renames. Start with a focused debug session on app/routers/students.py line 47 and app/auth/deps.py.
